newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Swiss president inaugurates Cambodian hospital.
newsitem.headline: Swiss president inaugurates Cambodian hospital.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk and Swiss President Jean Pascal Delamuraz on Saturday inaugurated a modern children's hospital funded by an anonymous donor.
Dr Beat Richner, driving force behind the Kantha Bopha II hospital, said the Swiss government had agreed to give medicine worth $500,000 to mark the hospital's inauguration.
The hospital has been built on land donated by the ailing Sihanouk, who was making his first public appearance in months.
Dr Peter Studer, an associate of Richner, said the 150-bed Kantha Bopha II was the most modern hospital in Cambodia and had been built and equipped with funds from an anonymous donor.
Kantha Bopha I and II, named after Sihanouk's infant daughter who died of leukaemia, have a combined staff of 560 and receive an annual $1 million subsidy from the Swiss government.
The Swiss president, who arrived earlier in the day to a royal welcome, said his visit marked the restoration of centuries-old ties between the two countries.

Delamuraz was to hold talks later with co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen. His schedule included signing of an investment promotion and protection accord to safeguard Swiss companies against possible future nationalisation of industry and allow free transfer of profits, officials said.

After a state dinner with King Norodom Sihanouk on Saturday, Delamuraz and his wife travel on Sunday to Siem Reap to visit the nearby 12th century Angkor Wat and other temples. He leaves Siem Reap for Bangkok on Monday.
